title: Correct finding with an incomplete proof of concept
scenario: The submitted PoC does not compile against the current commit, but the missing authorization check and the resulting cross-tenant read are both visible in the source and confirmed by a captured request pair.
exercises: an incomplete PoC does not refute a demonstrable behavior
execution confidence is reported separately from technical validity

mutations.name: a broken PoC is not a refutation
a demonstrable behavior is not unknown merely because the PoC failed
mutations.expect_error: adjudication.technical_claim is UNKNOWN but no unresolved question blocks that axis

challenged_finding.claimed_impact: Cross-tenant record disclosure through a missing authorization check

prosecutor.strongest_claim: The export endpoint resolves the tenant from the request body instead of the session, so any authenticated user can read another tenant's records.

attacker_capability.statement: Any authenticated user can call the export endpoint.

required_state.statement: A record exists under a different tenant id.

evidence.ref: captured response 200 with 412 foreign records, request id 7f2c9

execution_path.statement: The handler reads tenantId from the body and queries without comparing it to the session tenant.

violated_property.statement: A user reads only records belonging to their own tenant.

evidence.ref: src/api/export.ts:78 query lacks the session tenant predicate

impact.statement: Records of an arbitrary tenant are returned to the caller.

evidence.ref: captured response 200, request id 7f2c9, 412 foreign records

defender.strongest_counterargument: The PoC does not run against the current commit, so the behavior may already be fixed.

evidence.ref: report PoC fails to compile: missing exportClient import

challenges.statement: A middleware may enforce the tenant predicate before the handler executes.
The captured request pair may predate a fix on the current commit.
The returned records may be redacted downstream before reaching the client.
Authentication is required, so the attacker is not fully permissionless.
The foreign tenant id may have been guessable only in the test environment.

challenge_matrix.finding: The tenant middleware is mounted on /v1 only; the /v2 export route bypasses it.
The handler on the current commit still reads tenantId from the body.
Any authenticated user suffices; no elevated role is needed.
Tenant ids are sequential integers exposed in list responses.
The captured response contains unredacted foreign records.

assumptions.statement: The /v2 export route bypasses the tenant middleware.
The handler on the current commit still trusts the body tenantId.
The volume of exposed records matches the report's estimate across all tenants.

attack_path.transition: Attacker authenticates as an ordinary tenant user.
Attacker posts an export request carrying a foreign tenantId.
Handler queries by the body tenant id without the session predicate.
Attacker receives 412 records belonging to tenant 418.

counterexamples.reason: The tenant middleware would have blocked the request, but it is mounted only on the /v1 router.

decisive_facts.fact: The /v2 export handler reads tenantId from the request body on the current commit.
A captured response returns foreign-tenant records to an ordinary user.

severity_challenge.demonstrated_impact: Read access to another tenant's records by any authenticated user
severity_challenge.policy_alignment: Matches the program's unauthorized access to sensitive data tier for web assets.

adjudication.strongest_supporting_evidence: The handler queries by the body tenant id with no session predicate at src/api/export.ts:61-78.
adjudication.strongest_opposing_evidence: The submitted PoC does not compile against the current commit.
adjudication.rationale: The PoC is broken, but the source at the current commit and the captured request pair establish the behavior independently; a broken PoC is a reproduction problem, not a refutation.
